title: An invertible quotient unit gives the shifted completeness triangles
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A$, a uniformizer $t$, and any scheme $W$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $R=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/t^n)_W$ and $S_n=(A/t^n)_W$, restricted along the specified projections [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the unbounded derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $P$ be a flat-term K-flat complex representing $K\in D(R)$ [def-a1-flat-term-kflat-complex]. For the strict quotient tower $U(P)_n=P\otimes_R S_n$, with its quotient transitions [def-a1-principal-completed-koszul-towers], let
$$\eta_P:P\longrightarrow\mathsf C(U(P)),\qquad p\longmapsto(0,(p\otimes1)_n)$$
be the zero shifted-product augmentation in the coordinates $d(y,x)=(-dy-(1-s)x,dx)$ of [def-weil-strict-roos-model]. Suppose its image in $D(R)$ is an isomorphism. No completeness hypothesis on $K$ is imposed in addition to this specified-unit hypothesis.

For every $r\in\mathbf Z$, $P[r]$ is again flat-term K-flat. Under the total-tensor identification $U(P[r])=U(P)[r]$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the natural chain isomorphism
$$\sigma_r:\mathsf C(U(P[r]))\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathsf C(U(P))[r],\qquad(y,x)\longmapsto((-1)^r y,x)$$
satisfies $\sigma_r\eta_{P[r]}=\eta_P[r]$; its inverse has the same signs. Thus the image of $\eta_{P[r]}$ is an isomorphism. There is a distinguished triangle
$$K[r]\xrightarrow{(c_{r,n})_n}\prod_{n\geq1}^{D}K[r]_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_{n\geq1}^{D}K[r]_n\longrightarrow K[r+1],$$
where $K[r]_n=\operatorname{Res}_n(K[r]\otimes_R^LS_n)$ and $c_{r,n}$ are exactly the canonical derived reduction maps [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. This conclusion holds for the reduction system and its maps computed from every K-flat representative of $K[r]$, not just $P[r]$. In particular $K[r]$ is derived complete in the Roos-triangle sense of [def-weil-derived-complete]. No boundedness, constructibility, finiteness of $W$ or invertibility of $\ell$ on $W$ is required.
